newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile court jails ex-naval officer for spy book.
newsitem.headline: Chile court jails ex-naval officer for spy book.

text.p: Chile's Supreme Court has upheld a prison sentence against a former military officer for writing a book on naval intelligence, according to a court ruling released on Thursday.

The court sentenced ex-naval captain Humberto Palamara Iribarne on Tuesday to 61-day suspended jail term for the publication of the book "Ethics and Intelligence Services" and ordered the confiscation of 900 copies of the book.
Palmera Iribarne was convicted last year by a military court in the southern city of Punta Arenas of breaching of his naval duties and on two counts of disobedience.

The book's contents are unknown, but local media have speculated that it may give details of the role played by Chilean intelligence forces in the war between Britain and Argentina over the Falkland Islands in 1982.
Although Chile declared itself neutral in the conflict, some analysts have said that Santiago allowed British planes to land and ships to be supplied from Chilean territory.
The then-military government of General Augusto Pinochet denied the allegations.

The Supreme Court ruled that even though Palamara Iribarne wrote the book after he retired from naval service, he was still bound by military rules. The former captain served for two years as deputy head of the intelligence department in Chile's third naval zone.
